subject: Next steps: Purchasing path orchestration — commits vs on-demand for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Howard <rita.howard@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 15:22:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps: Purchasing path orchestration — commits vs on-demand for Acme Analytics

Thanks again for your time today, Rita — good conversation. Quick recap and three asks so we can align pricing and procurement language before you engage legal/finance:

Summary from the call:
- Primary use case: near-real-time inference for customer-facing scoring; initial pilot across 2 teams, then org-level rollout if latency and cost targets met.
- Deployment options discussed: Hosted (fast onboarding, per-token), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with commits), Private (VPC/on-prem for regulated data).
- Procurement signals: procurement favors PO for enterprise purchases; finance prefers committed spend if we can provide predictable unit economics and discounts.
- Marketplace: you asked whether we can go through the cloud marketplace for procurement ease — we can, but it changes billing flow and may affect committed pricing and SLA coverage.

Three asks (responses will shape the quote and SOW draft):
1) Which purchasing vehicle does procurement prefer in principle? (PO on Redwood invoice vs. Cloud marketplace listing vs. card for pilot)
2) For the production timeline, is finance open to a 12-month commit (we can model step-down discounts) or do you need on-demand pricing only for now?
3) Any mandatory compliance artifacts (SOC 2 type II, KMS/HSM, audit logs) beyond what we discussed? If yes, list owners.

Attachments: SOW_sample_hosted_vs_dedicated.pdf (high-level SOW options), pricing_grid_q1_2026.xlsx (starter numbers).

Suggested next step: 30-minute procurement check-in with Tom + your procurement lead this week to confirm PO vs marketplace and commit appetite. I can share a short procurement checklist in advance.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Rita Howard <rita.howard@acme-analytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:11:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Purchasing path orchestration — commits vs on-demand for Acme Analytics

Kim, great recap — thanks. Quick answers below; appreciate the attachments.

1) Purchasing vehicle: Procurement prefers PO routed through our AP process. Marketplace is acceptable only if pricing is identical and procurement can track spend centrally; otherwise they will push for PO. For the pilot we can use card spend (~USD 5k) to move faster but anything above that needs PO.

2) Commit vs on-demand: Finance is open to a 12-month commit for the production rollout if we can lock in predictable unit costs and a cap on overage pricing. Pilot will be on-demand. We need a clear migration path from pilot card/on-demand to committed Dedicated or Hosted with commit.

3) Compliance: SOC 2 Type II report required; customer-managed KMS is preferred for production (we need HSM/KMS options documented). Also need confirmation of data residency controls (log retention and encryption at rest). Owners: Tom Sanders (IT procurement) and Priya Mehta (Security) — I've cc'd Tom but will loop Priya in once we have a prelim SOW.

Can we do a short call TUE/WED of this week (US PST) to run through the procurement checklist and show the pricing spreadsheet to finance?

Thanks,
Rita

--
Rita Howard
Director, Procurement | Acme Analytics
rita.howard@acme-analytics.com | +1 (617) 444-9200
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Rita Howard <rita.howard@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Purchasing path orchestration — commits vs on-demand for Acme Analytics

Looping in a brief pricing/ops recommendation from our side to shape the SOW that fits Acme's procurement constraints. Key points: 

- Pilot (card/on-demand): recommend Hosted API with constrained quota for initial months (cheap to stand up, no infra lead time). We can throttle tokens and attach per-route budgets to prevent surprise spend.

- Production (PO + commit): recommend Dedicated reserved pool with 12-month commit. Benefits: predictable throughput, lower per-token cost at scale, and clear SLA. We'll provide a pricing matrix that shows break-even point vs hosted on-demand and present a migration path.

- Marketplace option: possible if procurement requires it for approval workflows, but note: marketplace billing often prevents applying our standard committed discounts and complicates SLAs. If procurement insists, Finance should accept a smaller discount or a hybrid (commit on Redwood + marketplace for ancillary services).

- Compliance deliverables: we can provide SOC 2 type II attestation, and we support customer-managed KMS for private deployments; Marcus, can you confirm HSM/KMS doc location and expected turnaround for providing a technical addendum?

Attached: dedicated_commit_pricing_v2.pdf — includes a 12-month reserved configuration and migration milestones (pilot -> canary -> prod).

Actionable next steps proposed:
1) Book a procurement/IT 30-min sync with Acme (include Tom & Priya) to confirm PO vs marketplace + KMS needs.
2) We draft a preliminary SOW (hosted vs dedicated paths) and a clean migration annex for the pilot-to-commit timeline.
3) Prep a short one-page doc for Finance showing unit economics and break-even for 12-month commit vs on-demand.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Rita Howard <rita.howard@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Sanders <tom.sanders@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Next steps: Purchasing path orchestration — commits vs on-demand for Acme Analytics

Thanks, Rita & Tom — this is helpful and gives us a clean path. Quick recap and proposed schedule so your team can circulate internally: 

Recap:
- Pilot: Hosted on-demand via card (~$5k cap) for initial 6 weeks. Redwood will apply quota limits and spend alerts.
- Production: PO + 12-month Dedicated commit is recommended by Redwood for predictable cost and SLA; we will include a migration annex in the SOW.
- Marketplace: acceptable if procurement requires it, but discounts and SLA terms differ — we'll prepare a marketplace appendix that maps differences.
- Compliance: we will provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and technical KMS/HSM addendum. Marcus will share the KMS doc in the procurement packet.

Immediate next steps (owners & timing):
1) Procurement sync (30 min) — owners: Rita / Tom / Kimberly (Redwood) — target: Thu, 15 Jan, 10:00–10:30 PST. I'll send the invite once you confirm.
2) Redwood to deliver: (a) short procurement checklist, (b) SOW draft with pilot -> dedicated migration annex, (c) one-page finance economics — owners: Ben (pricing), Marcus (KMS addendum) — delivery by Fri EOD 16 Jan.
3) If procurement requests marketplace routing, Redwood will produce the marketplace appendix showing billing, discount delta, and SLA implications — owner: Ben — delivery within 2 business days after request.

If this looks good, Rita, please confirm the Thu slot and whether Priya Mehta (security) should join the sync; Tom, please share Priya's email and any procurement intake form we should prefill.

Thanks — Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
